counting_rule: Two existing candidates developed to the same diligence dimensions as BLU3797. Additional reports, source audits, competitors and model routes are not new lead discoveries or newly performed experiments.

candidate_updates.name: Enasidenib for germline IDH2-R140Q D2HGA2
candidate_updates.decision: Defined clinical development priority: recommend a bounded pediatric article/exposure project linked to prospective organ function.
candidate_updates.priority_scope: Clinical-stage work queue; no numerical cross-program success probability or asset-return rank.
candidate_updates.exact_entity: Enasidenib; mesylate tablet reference and documented pediatric sprinkle use. Intended infant presentation must be specified; historical clinical lot identity with EP4058028B1 is unverified.
candidate_updates.population: Direct human treatment anchor is germline heterozygous IDH2-R140Q. R140G, type-I D2HGDH disease and other IDH2 variants do not inherit efficacy.
candidate_updates.functional_evidence: One clear severe-cardiomyopathy trajectory: LVEF 20–25% at entry, 35–40% at six months and 40–45% at eight months with later fluctuation and concurrent care. A second original child had normal baseline systolic function; Gold had milder baseline disease. Biochemical suppression is strong; neurological outcomes are less causally secure.
candidate_updates.biological_units: Five outcome case records across three publications; original two and Gold are clearly distinct. Cross-publication linkage of two skin cases is unresolved. Metadata-only five-week-old report adds zero verified outcomes.
candidate_updates.material_route: Defined marketed tablet and research free-base routes; actual studied sprinkle and concrete minitablet patent. Public route and historical use do not establish received lot, present supply or infant administration compatibility.
candidate_updates.model_route: ATCC R140Q TF-1/parent route is biochemical, homozygous and cancer-line specific. Endogenous heterozygous mouse and genetic reversibility precedents exist. A new human cardiac model is optional when it discriminates a consequential exposure/function question.
candidate_updates.exposure_and_safety: Current adult PK includes 7.9-day half-life, tenfold accumulation, 29-day steady state, active metabolite, interactions and plausible A3 antagonism. No infant dose rule or lifelong safety boundary. Direct pediatric ALT/CK observations require a coherent longitudinal exposure/laboratory timeline.
candidate_updates.public_rights_and_contribution: Existing clinical program and published granted pediatric minitablet composition/process claims prevent a first-pediatric-formulation or open-rights claim. Define an improvement in delivery, exposure, burden/tolerability or prospective clinical evidence; standalone value capture remains unresolved.
candidate_updates.deciding_proof: Qualify one intended pediatric article/administration route and parent/metabolite/chiral-D2HG measures, then link exposure to observed tolerability and a preselected growth-aware organ outcome with suitable comparison and concurrent-care accounting.
candidate_updates.advance_condition: Reliable delivery and interpretable exposure/PD plus a useful organ-function or preservation signal justify confirmation; a larger product program requires independently supported clinical benefit and a real product advantage.
candidate_updates.stop_or_redirect_condition: Redirect delivery failure or exposure-related harm; narrow tissue/genotype/timing claims when appropriate. Do not reject human observations from an unqualified model. Stop a standalone product thesis if no useful incremental contribution or practicable product route exists.
candidate_updates.round7_delta: Full clinical lineage and 177-cell laboratory audit; specific public pediatric formulation, adult PK/DDI/A3 and model audit; staged clinical proof with independent challenge. Removed from the reserve list to avoid conflicting current dispositions.

candidate_updates.name: Ruxolitinib 1.5% cream for refractory Hailey–Hailey disease
candidate_updates.decision: Defined controlled clinical-proof priority: recommend marketed-article, protocol and measurement qualification followed by a contemporaneously controlled patient-benefit comparison.
candidate_updates.priority_scope: Clinical-stage work queue; not an established proprietary asset or numerical cross-program investment rank.
candidate_updates.exact_entity: Prospective standardized Opzelura 1.5% cream, 15 mg/g ruxolitinib base equivalent as 19.8 mg/g phosphate. Historical cases verify active/concentration/route, not every brand, vehicle or lot.
candidate_updates.functional_evidence: Five distinguishable exact-strength case reports support useful local control. Monotherapy-style treatment, add-on induction and topical maintenance are kept separate. No controlled exact-rux HHD effect estimate was verified.
candidate_updates.biological_units: Five selected single-patient reports, not a consecutive treated denominator. EADV duplicate and separate 1%+naltrexone report excluded from that count. Nine-patient preprint remains abstract-only and unpooled.
candidate_updates.material_route: Manufactured marketed cream defines a clinical article. Research free base/phosphate are assay routes, not equivalent clinical formulations. Qualified matched vehicle is one option; pragmatic randomized whole-product add-on comparison is a defined alternative.
candidate_updates.model_route: ATP2C1 engineered/organotypic research precedents, with parent identity and assay-stage limits. Optional mechanism work only; immune-free model negativity cannot rule out an inflammatory clinical mechanism.
candidate_updates.exposure_and_safety: AD PK: 479-person 1.5% phaseIII subgroup, mean Css 35.7 nM; maximum-use n=40 mean 104 nM with high-exposure extremes. No HHD PK boundary. 281 nM is a laboratory proxy, not a universal safety threshold; follow current label/combination context.
candidate_updates.public_rights_and_contribution: Existing composition/formulation claims and branded franchise; current ANDA litigation. KB111 and guselkumab are active distinct HHD programs. Controlled data may be valuable, while a proprietary asset needs a differentiated benefit and executable rights/manufacturing/regulatory route.
candidate_updates.deciding_proof: Prespecified patient-level clinical estimand with concurrent care/control, masked lesion assessment, meaningful pain/recurrence/rescue/burden interpretation and exposure linked to applied grams, active erosion and healing. No forced withdrawal or automatic new-model gate.
candidate_updates.advance_condition: Controlled useful clinical benefit or comparable efficacy with a meaningful burden/tolerability advantage, interpretable exposure and acceptable observed safety; exploratory evidence can justify independent confirmation.
candidate_updates.stop_or_redirect_condition: Rule out a meaningful benefit only with an informative design and adequate delivery; redirect measurement/article failures. Stop the proposed product for reproducible unacceptable effective-exposure harm or no differentiated product contribution.
candidate_updates.round7_delta: Five-report clinical audit, DERM101 concurrent-control benchmark, mechanistic citation correction, quantitative PK/high-exposure and official-patent audit, current competitors and a staged clinical proof. No new lead counted.

accepted_review_refinements: Historical sprinkle lot/patent identity not inferred
Infant and HHD exposure tolerability limited to observed follow-up
Rux controlled window harmonized to 8–12-week planning assumption
One primary value dimension; no required superiority on every secondary endpoint
Responder-enriched maintenance and rescue/missingness handling explicit
Label combination/BSA context retained without treating it as an HHD safety boundary
open_access_limits: Nine-patient HHD preprint abstract-only; public dataset embargo retained
HHD final actin-model paper indexed sections plus full earlier preprint; no independent replication inferred
